name: DA-2K
ability_definition: The ability to judge which of several objects is closer or farther away from you, or to judge the distance between you and an object.

task_realism.reasoning: Deciding which of two points in a real photograph is closer directly exercises the 'which object is closer' half of the ability. The eight scene types (indoor, outdoor, aerial, underwater, transparent/reflective) add real variety. However, real work that uses depth perception (driving, operating equipment, catching or placing objects, surveying) happens in live 3D space from the person's own viewpoint, not in single still images annotated by others.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Inputs are static monocular images with no stereo, motion parallax, or active viewpoint change. There is no time pressure and no consequence for errors. Point pairs are curated and human-verified, which may over-sample tricky cases compared with typical work. Real tasks usually involve continuous judgments during movement, with feedback.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers only ordinal relative depth between two points. It does not test the second half of the ability, estimating absolute distance from the viewer. It also does not test ordering among several objects, gauging gaps between objects, or judging depth of moving targets. The scene diversity is good, but the construct slice is narrow.

format_match.reasoning: The output is a forced binary choice between two pre-marked pixels. Real work rarely presents depth questions this way. Workers make implicit, continuous distance judgments that feed into actions (steering, reaching, positioning), not explicit closer/farther labels on photos.

transferability_reasoning: DA-2K cleanly tests relative 'which is closer' judgments across diverse real-world scene types, so it captures one core part of depth perception. It omits metric distance estimation, multi-object ordering, and the dynamic, binocular, action-coupled conditions of real work, and it uses an artificial binary point-pair format. Transfer to workplace depth-perception capability is therefore moderate to limited.

2025.human_reference: General adult population, since ordinal depth judgment from images is a universal perceptual ability and not a specialist skill.
